# Steering bump stops and clunks

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Turn steering fully on an incline while listening for a distinct clunk at full lock. [t2019]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Turn the steering wheel fully to one side while driving on an incline or unlevel ground.
2. Listen for a distinct clunking sound that occurs only at full lock.

_Procedure reported by [t2019]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Inspect both sides of the vehicle, as there are two bump stops per side arranged in diagonally opposite pairs (one on the driver's side and one on the passenger's side). [t2019]
- Look for shiny metal surfaces where plastic caps should be present. [t2019]
- Apply synthetic grease to the contact points between the stop and the control arm. [t2019]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Checking only one side of the vehicle, missing the diagonally opposite partner bump stop. [t2019]
